LFA 1000 Laser Flash Apparatus (Thermal Conductivity / Diffusivity)
Product catalog summary
Introduction
LINSEIS Corporation, established in 1957, is a leader in thermal analysis, known for high-quality standards and customer satisfaction across sectors like polymers, chemicals, and environmental analytics.
Technique Overview
The flash method is used for measuring thermal diffusivity and conductivity, offering non-contact measurement, small sample size, and high accuracy. The LFA 1000 series is a cost-effective solution for temperatures from -125°C to 1600°C.
Measurement Concept
The LFA 1000 uses a sample robot and furnace setup. A programmable energy pulse causes a temperature rise, measured by an IR detector. Thermal diffusivity and specific heat are calculated, and thermal conductivity is derived if density is known.
Absolute Method
The LFA 1000 employs an absolute measurement technique, eliminating the need for system calibration, and complies with standards like ASTM E-1461 and DIN 30905.
System Design
The system features a vertical arrangement for easy handling and optimal results, with adjustable pulse energy and duration for various sample types.
Future Upgrades
The modular design allows for upgrades in temperature range and detectors, providing flexibility for future needs.
Detectors and Environmental Options
The system supports InSb and MCT detectors, covering a wide temperature range, and can operate under specific atmospheric conditions with options for vacuum or gas dosing systems.
Vision Control
This feature ensures high signal quality for different sample sizes, overcoming positioning issues with zoom lens systems.
Sample Throughput
The LFA 1000 offers high sample throughput, capable of measuring up to 18 samples in a few hours.
Software
The software is compatible with MS Windows, offering features like data security, curve comparison, and multi-method analysis, supporting automatic and manual data input and model selection for evaluation.
Specific Heat Determination
Specific heat is calculated by comparing the temperature rise of a sample to a reference under identical conditions.
Technical Data
The LFA 1000 operates in a temperature range from -100°C to 1600°C, with high accuracy and repeatability for thermal diffusivity and specific heat measurements.
Applications
The LFA 1000 is used for measuring thermal properties of materials like graphite and glass ceramics, providing reliable data for industrial applications.
Thermal Properties of Graphite
Graphite's thermal diffusivity was measured from room temperature to 1600°C. Results showed a linear decrease in thermal conductivity and a plateau in thermal diffusivity above 500°C, with specific heat capacity slightly increasing with temperature.
Thermal Properties of Glass Ceramics
For glass ceramics, both thermal diffusivity and conductivity slightly decreased with temperature, while specific heat capacity increased. Pyroceram demonstrated reproducibility with a variation within +/- 1% up to 1250°C.
Influence of Sample Thickness
Accuracy of thermal conductivity measurements was investigated using silver samples of varying thickness. Accuracy decreases exponentially with smaller sample diameters, with a critical threshold around 200 micrometers.
Contact Information
Contact details for LINSEIS GmbH and its international branches are provided, offering various products and services related to thermal analysis.
